marble.name: Scaled picture and bar graphs
marble.subject: Mathematics
marble.description: Draw a scaled picture graph and a scaled bar graph to represent a data set; solve one- and two-step comparison, sum, and difference problems using bar charts, pictograms, and tables
marble.prompt: If you looked at a bar chart showing how many books different children read last month, could they work out the total, find the difference between the most and least, and draw their own chart with a scale like "each square = 2 books"?

cluster.summary: Your child is learning to organise and count information by sorting objects into groups and comparing which groups have more or fewer items.

misconceptions: Ignores the scale and reads each square/symbol as one unit (or just counts symbols)
Cannot read an intermediate value — rounds a mid-interval bar to a gridline or ignores a part-symbol
Collapses a two-step problem to one step (reads a value but doesn't combine, or does the wrong operation)
Constructs a scaled axis with unequal intervals, so positions no longer map to values
representations: Scaled bar graph on squared paper (each square = 2/5/10)
Scaled pictogram with a stated key and part-symbols
Frequency table as the source, with the scale chosen from the largest value
Two bars aligned for a difference, or stacked for a sum
authoredAnswer: Interpreting: reads values through the stated key; with one symbol=10 children, half a symbol=5 children. Gives the difference for how many more. A numerical bar midpoint between10 and15 is12½ when that quantity is meaningful, never rounded to12 or13 without an explicit rounding instruction. Translating: draws bars for20 and15 from a common baseline with equal widths and uniform intervals, for example each square=5;

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Child reads 3 football symbols as 3 rather than 15
wrongAnswers.fix: Read the key aloud first; overlay the count each symbol carries; re-read via multiplication by the scale

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Child reads a half-symbol as a whole, or a bar halfway between 10 and 15 as 10 or 15
wrongAnswers.fix: Show half a symbol = half the key; count the sub-intervals of the scale to read between gridlines

wrongAnswers.revealedBy: Child gives a single value for 'total of the top two', or subtracts when a sum is needed
wrongAnswers.fix: Scaffold the two steps explicitly: read each value, then decide sum or difference and do it
